questions.stem: The bulk modulus of a liquid is $2 \times 10^9\ \mathrm{N/m^2}$. The fractional compression in volume ($\Delta V/V$) required to increase the pressure of the liquid by $2 \times 10^6\ \mathrm{N/m^2}$ is:
questions.solution:
Bulk Modulus $B = \frac{\Delta P}{\Delta V/V}$.
Thus, $\frac{\Delta V}{V} = \frac{\Delta P}{B} = \frac{2 \times 10^6}{2 \times 10^9} = 10^{-3}$.

questions.stem: A wire of length $L$ and area of cross-section $A$ is made of material of Young's modulus $Y$. It is stretched by an amount $x$. The work done in stretching the wire is $W = \frac{Y A x^2}{k L}$. The value of $k$ is _________.
questions.solution:
The work done in stretching a wire is $W = \frac{1}{2} F x = \frac{1}{2} \left(\frac{Y A x}{L}\right) x = \frac{Y A x^2}{2 L}$.
Comparing with the given formula, $k = 2$.

questions.stem: A wire of length $L$ and radius $r$ is clamped rigidly at one end. When a pulling force $F$ is applied at the other end, its elongation is $l$. If another wire of the same material but of length $2L$ and radius $2r$ is stretched by the same force $F$, then its elongation will be:
questions.solution:
Elongation is $l = \frac{FL}{A Y} = \frac{FL}{\pi r^2 Y}$.
For the second wire, $l' = \frac{F(2L)}{\pi (2r)^2 Y} = \frac{2 FL}{4 \pi r^2 Y} = \frac{l}{2}$.

questions.stem: A wire of length $L$ and cross-sectional area $A$ is made of a material of Young's modulus $Y$. If the wire is stretched by an amount $x$, the work done in stretching the wire is:
questions.solution:
The work done in stretching a wire is stored as elastic potential energy: $W = \frac{1}{2} F x$.
Since $F = \frac{Y A x}{L}$,
$W = \frac{1}{2} \left(\frac{Y A x}{L}\right) x = \frac{YAx^2}{2L}$.

questions.stem: The bulk modulus of a liquid is $3 \times 10^9\ \mathrm{N/m^2}$. To reduce the volume of the liquid by $1\%$, the fractional pressure change needed is:
questions.solution:
Bulk modulus $B = -\frac{\Delta P}{\Delta V/V}$.
Given $\frac{\Delta V}{V} = -1\% = -0.01$.
$\Delta P = B \left( -\frac{\Delta V}{V} \right) = 3 \times 10^9 \times 0.01 = 3 \times 10^7\ \mathrm{N/m^2}$.
